lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Good morning, welcome to the Harbour View Hotel. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: I would like a double room for two nights from Friday 12 June.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: We have one double room left on the third floor, and it overlooks the garden.

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: That sounds suitable. My surname is Marston, M-A-R-S-T-O-N.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Thank you, Ms Marston. The room is eighty-four pounds a night, including breakfast.

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Could we check in at eleven? Our train arrives at ten thirty.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Normal check-in is from two, but early check-in is available for an extra ten pounds.

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: We will pay for early check-in. Could we also book dinner for seven, sorry, make that eight, as our train may be delayed.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Certainly. Dinner at eight is booked, and I have noted that you need a quiet room away from the lift.

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Do you provide towels for the swimming pool?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Yes, pool towels are free at reception, but guests pay a five-pound deposit for a locker key.

lines.speaker: Guest
lines.text: Perfect. Could you send the confirmation to my email address, please?

clips.title: Section 2: Introduction to the Milltown Summer Festival

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: Welcome to this introduction to the Milltown Summer Festival, which takes place from Friday 18 July to Sunday 20 July.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: This year the festival has moved from the market square to Riverside Park because we expect more visitors.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: The main stage will be beside the lake, and local bands will perform from midday until ten in the evening.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: On Saturday morning, there will be a farmers' market with more than forty stalls selling bread, cheese and flowers.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: Visitors who enjoy cooking should not miss the demonstration by chef Ana Ruiz at three on Saturday afternoon.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: For children, the story tent opens at ten each morning, and each session lasts forty-five minutes.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: A free bus will run every twenty minutes from the railway station to the main entrance.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: If you drive, the car park on Mill Road has space for 300 cars, but it usually fills before noon.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: The festival's information office is in a green cabin near the main entrance, where visitors can collect a map.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: On Sunday, the parade begins at eleven, sorry, at twelve, because the fun run uses the High Street until late morning.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: Most events are free, although tickets for the evening concert cost twelve pounds for adults and six pounds for children.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: In case of heavy rain, outdoor performances will move to the community hall on Bridge Street.

lines.speaker: Presenter
lines.text: We are still looking for volunteers to help at the information office on Sunday afternoon.

clips.title: Section 3: Planning a presentation on urban bees

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: For our presentation, we agreed to focus on how city gardens help urban bees.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Yes, and Professor Carter asked us to include data from at least three recent studies.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I found a study from 2022 that surveyed 150 gardens across the city.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: I can summarise the methods, and you could explain the results.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Good idea. We also need one clear chart, so I will prepare a bar chart showing flower types.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: Our presentation is on Wednesday, no, Thursday, because the seminar room is unavailable on Wednesday.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: It lasts twenty minutes, including five minutes for questions.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: We should mention that bees preferred gardens with native plants.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: The strongest result was a 30 per cent increase in bee visits where native flowers were planted.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: I will bring the handouts, but we should upload the slides by Tuesday evening.

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: Let us practise in the library tomorrow at four.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: I cannot do four; I have a lab session until five, so shall we meet at half past five?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: That works. Please bring the printed references.

lines.speaker: Leo
lines.text: And I will email Professor Carter tonight to confirm the title.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Today I will discuss how sustainable buildings reduce energy use without sacrificing comfort.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: A key principle is passive design, which uses the position of a building to capture sunlight and natural breezes.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: In warm climates, wide roof overhangs shade windows and keep indoor temperatures lower.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: In colder regions, thick insulation in the walls and roof prevents heat from escaping.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Many new buildings collect rainwater from the roof and use it to flush toilets.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Solar panels are now common, but in the case study, geothermal heating supplied most of the winter heating.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: The case study is a library in Denmark, completed in 2019, with space for 2,000 visitors.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Its windows face south, allowing winter sunlight to warm the reading rooms.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Sensors adjust the blinds automatically when the sunlight becomes too strong.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Recycled steel was used for the frame, while local timber formed the interior panels.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: The building uses 40 per cent less energy than a conventional library, which uses 250 units per square metre each year.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: At the end of its life, many parts can be taken apart and reused, a principle known as design for disassembly.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Next week, we will compare this library with a school in Australia.

lines.speaker: Lecturer
lines.text: Students should read chapter seven before the seminar and note one feature they would change.
